title: Five A.M.
logline: Five in the morning, a silent kitchen, the first quiet minutes before a long study session. Every sound of the ritual with {product}, from frost to the crack to the fizz, heard up close.

world.setting: A dark walnut kitchen counter with a slate top at 5am, a window of cool blue pre-dawn light to one side, one warm under-cabinet light, a notebook and pencil waiting at the end of the counter.
world.palette: Dark walnut, black slate and cool pre-dawn blue, so the can's sky blue, silver and red carry all the colour; the warm under-cabinet light is the one accent.
world.rules: No packaging, appliances or labels in frame except the product. The notebook page shows only unreadable pencil scribble shapes.

locations.name: The 5am counter
locations.plate_prompt: Photoreal vertical 9:16 location plate: a dark walnut kitchen counter with a black slate top at 5am, cool blue pre-dawn light from a window on the left, one warm under-cabinet light strip glowing at the back, a small black stone bowl of crushed ice, an empty tall clear glass, and at the far end a closed notebook with a blank cover and a pencil. Very clean, calm, minimal. No people, no packaging, no readable text, no brands.

beats.summary: Silence, then a fingertip drags a slow squeaking line through the frost on the can. A whisper: listen.
The ritual: a steel scoop through crushed ice, the can settled into the ice, two soft taps on the full can.
The hero sound: a nail under the tab, half a second of silence, the crack, the mist, the fizz up close.
The pour over clear ice, cubes crackling, bubbles rising in slow motion.
One sip, a soft exhale, the brand whispered; then the pencil starts scratching: the study session begins.
The can alone on the slate, one drop rolling down; the tagline whispered.

lore: Imani Brooks is a second-year public health grad student renting the top floor of a 1920s brick row house in West Philadelphia. Her qualifying exam is in six days.

The counter is a salvaged walnut slab from a closed neighbourhood bakery, topped with a honed black slate board; she oils the walnut every Sunday and the slate still carries a pale water ring from the first week.
She has kept the same ritual for 41 mornings in a row: 5am, one can over crushed ice, one page of pencil notes before the sun comes up. The notebook is the fifth Aldercroft notebook this semester.
The basalt ice bowl was her grandmother's; it is rough and pitted outside and polished smooth inside from decades of use.
The radiator knocks twice at 5:03 every morning; that is her cue to open the can.
